newsitem.title: JAPAN: TSE head to visit China's securities authority.
newsitem.headline: TSE head to visit China's securities authority.

text.p: The Tokyo Stock Exchange (TSE) said on Thursday that its president Mitsuhide Yamaguchi will meet China Securities Regulatory Commission chairman Zhou Daojiong during his three-day visit to China, beginning on December 4.
The meeting is expected to touch on preparations for listing Chinese companies' shares on the TSE.
Japanese government sources said earlier that Tokyo and Beijing will likely exchange notes which will pave the way for Chinese companies to list on the Japanese stock exchange within a few months.
The TSE has seen a steady decline in the number of issues listed on its foreign section, and has eased listing requirements in order to lure Asian companies on to the exchange.
The number of listed firms on the TSE's foreign section has fallen to 67 from a peak of 127 firms in 1991.
